story: On a sunny Thursday evening at 6:17 in Sumter Oaks, Gary is content at the parade sign-up table in the Town Square, looking over the entry rules while Rosa heads toward Magnolia Loop. Out on the street, Hal is dutifully counting the flamingos from the curb for the committee file, while Donna, sheepish but cheerful, has just promised him she'll narrow the flamingo flock down to three before Friday dinner.
events: Gary (parade signup table): Look over the sign-up sheet and entry rules for the parade
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos from the curb and note the tally for the committee file
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Rosa already answered me: dinner Friday at six, and I'm covered on the cornbread. Nothing left to ask her, and repeating myself would just be chatter. My real goal is the golf cart for the parade, and the parade_signup_table is right here in the square. I'll check what's needed to enter, which also keeps me mindful that any visible lights or sound system mods need Architectural Review approval under L-01 and Hal is already looking over my paperwork.

parameters.content: Look over the sign-up sheet and entry rules for the parade

donna.thought_process: Hal's counting my flamingos again and threatening the clipboard. L-02 says three visible from the street, and I'm over, no sense arguing the law. Friday dinner is tomorrow at six, I don't want a citation hanging over it, and I want Hal cheering at the courts for Gary's practice. Best move is to charm him, promise to trim the flock tonight, and keep him friendly. Then I'll go deal with the flamingos before the sun goes down.

parameters.content: Alright, alright, you got me, Hal. I'll have it down to three before Friday dinner, so keep that clipboard in the drawer and save your appetite and your cheering voice for tomorrow.

hal.thought_process: Donna just invited me to witness Gary's first practice at ten tomorrow, and I already gave her the flamingo count last tick. Repeating myself would be nagging. The flock is right here, so a proper tally for the committee file is in order. Count them myself, get the number on paper, and then I can show up at the courts tomorrow with facts instead of squinting from the curb. And if Gary's cart paperwork comes up, I'll help him get it right.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos from the curb and note the tally for the committee file

rosa.thought_process: Gary already answered me last tick and said he'll bring cornbread, so there's no need to ask him again. Hal and Donna are confirmed too, and the dinner is basically set. What's left is the actual prep: a table that seats four, groceries, and plates. The Town Square has nothing I need for that, so I should head home toward Magnolia Loop and get the house ready instead of lingering.

parameters.content: Heading home to get the table and kitchen ready for Friday's dinner.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
